memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient presents with epilepsy, asthma, and obesity.
She reports two generalized tonic‑clonic seizures in the past month, occasional wheeze and exertional dyspnoea, and struggles with weight control. On exam she is alert, BMI 32 kg/m2, blood pressure 118/72, respiratory rate 18, SpO2 98% room air. Chest clear, no wheeze. Neurologically normal. Spirometry shows FEV1 2.30 L (78% predicted), FVC 2.80 L, FEV1/FVC 0.82. Asthma Control Test score 16 (not well controlled). Smoking status: never. Inhaler technique checked: correct.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: EEG: background activity normal for age. No epileptiform discharges or focal slowing noted. No clinical correlation with recent seizures; study interpreted as normal.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling tired after my shifts and sometimes my chest feels tight when I climb the bus stairs. I’m worried about gaining more weight.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Patient reports no seizures since last visit, mild occasional wheeze after exertion, and weight stable at 88 kg. Asthma symptoms improved; uses salbutamol <2 times/week. Exam: BMI 31.5, BP 122/74, lungs clear. Spirometry: FEV1 2.55 L (87% predicted, +0.25 L from baseline), FVC 2.95 L, FEV1/FVC 0.86. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Smoking status never. Inhaler technique correct.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Spirometry with reversibility: Pre‑bronchodilator FEV1 2.55 L (87% predicted), FVC 2.95 L, FEV1/FVC 0.86. Post‑salbutamol FEV1 2.78 L (+0.23 L, 9% increase), FVC 3.10 L. Significant bronchodilator response confirming asthma.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2025-10-20 at 10:00 for pulmonary review with Dr Suresh Menon.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Patient reports seizure‑free for 4 months, asthma well controlled with no night symptoms, and weight down to 84 kg after lifestyle changes. She notes mild abdominal discomfort after meals. Exam: BMI 29.8, BP 118/70, lungs clear. Spirometry: FEV1 2.70 L (92% predicted, +0.15 L from last), FVC 3.20 L, FEV1/FVC 0.84. ACT score 24 (well controlled). Smoking never. Inhaler technique correct.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Gastroenterology for evaluation of mild transaminase elevation, possible NAFLD, given obesity and metabolic risk factors.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastroenterology review: ultrasound shows hepatic steatosis, no fibrosis. Advised lifestyle modification, weight control, and repeat LFT in 3 months. No pharmacologic therapy needed at this time.
